fields.title: What Happens Behind the Scenes
fields.keyTakeaway: When people and processes are involved in a service, the problem in front of the customer's eyes usually originates behind the scenes. A Blueprint shows this connection, and without it, you are fixing a symptom on display.
fields.checkQuestion: A customer complains that an answer arrives on the third day. Where should you look for the cause?
fields.blocks/0/text: Continuing the same question for the case when **the product is not just an interface**, but also the people, processes, and systems around it.
fields.blocks/1/subtitle: A journey map plus everything invisible to the customer
fields.blocks/1/items/0: **Customer actions** — the top layer, same as in CJM.
fields.blocks/1/items/1: **Frontstage employee actions** — what the customer observes: a support response, a phone call.
fields.blocks/1/items/2: **Backstage employee actions** — what happens behind the scenes: checks, approvals, manual operations.
fields.blocks/1/items/3: **Systems and processes** — what is involved, where data moves manually.
fields.blocks/1/items/4: **Line of visibility** — the boundary between what the customer sees and what they do not. Problems are usually born below it.
fields.blocks/2/text:
Complaint: “you write to support — they answer on the third day.”

Above the line of visibility, everything looks simple: an email was sent, there is no reply.

Below: the ticket drops into a shared inbox, an operator exports it to a spreadsheet once a day, questions about calculating hours go to the company accountant, and the accountant replies once every two days because it is not their main job.

Fixing the support interface was pointless: the three days were built from two manual handoffs behind the line of visibility.
fields.blocks/2/title: Smena: three days for a response
fields.blocks/3/text: A Blueprint is needed where people and manual processes are involved; for a fully self-serve product, it degenerates into an architecture diagram. And it is heavy: drawing it for the entire product takes weeks, so teams take one problematic scenario.
